title: Same model, wrong year
explanation: **Cause: year-level look-alikes, and possibly a dataset label error.** The photo shows the 2011+ Odyssey design (the stepped 'lightning-bolt' window line), which is exactly what the 2012 reference shows; the 2007 reference has a straight beltline. Either the image is mislabelled in Stanford Cars or the year cue is too subtle. Grad-CAM spreads over the wheels and rear window line, i.e. the body shape. **What VeriCar does:** for a claim of a 2007 Odyssey this becomes PARTIAL/MISMATCH, so the officer checks documents.

title: Confident, wrong make
explanation: **Cause: badge engineering.** The Chrysler Aspen is a rebadged Dodge Durango: same body, doors, glasshouse and wheels. In a pure side view the only distinguishing part (the grille) is hidden, so even a 100%-confident model has nothing to separate them; Grad-CAM sits on the shared rear quarter and C-pillar. **Lesson:** confidence is not identity for twin vehicles; a front-view photo is needed. This pair is a natural 'hard clone' case for our verification study.

title: Detector boxed the wrong region
explanation: **Cause: unusual viewpoint + wrong ROI.** An aerial, top-down shot with motion blur; Stanford Cars training images are almost all ground-level side / three-quarter views. The detector's box (red) covers mostly road, so the crop the classifier sees is a tall strip that gets squashed to a square. Confidence is only 27%, and re-running the full app pipeline even returns a different class, so the prediction is unstable. **What VeriCar does:** low confidence means LOW_CONFIDENCE / INSPECT, never MATCH.

title: Low light
explanation: **Cause: same-make look-alikes under poor light and occlusion.** Rolls-Royce Phantom and Ghost share the grille, lamps and proportions; at night with glare and a person standing in the open door, the side profile (the main difference) is hidden. Grad-CAM focuses on the grille, which both models share. Confidence is 43%. **What VeriCar does:** below the MATCH bar the verdict is INSPECT, and the make level (Rolls-Royce) is still verified.

title: Car cut off by the frame
explanation: **Cause: truncated side view.** Both bumpers are cut off by the frame, so the grille and lamps that separate Audi from BMW are missing; Grad-CAM attends to the soft top and windscreen frame, which look alike across small convertibles. Confidence is only 22%. **What VeriCar does:** LOW_CONFIDENCE in identify mode (top-3 shown) and INSPECT for a verification claim.
